entries.question: Using ordinary least-squares regression of the annual count of distinct fire events (unique Event_ID per year) against year, over 1984-2022, what is the slope in fires per year? Count only wildfire events (Incid_Type = 1).
entries.response:
Based on ordinary least-squares regression over the 1984–2022 period, the slope is **5.63 fires per year**. 

| slope | r_squared | p_value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5.63 | 0.149 | 0.015 |

This indicates an average increase of about 5.6 wildfire events per year over the study period.

entries.question: Compare the mean annual number of distinct fire events in the first decade of the record (1984-1993) with the last decade (2013-2022). Report the ratio last-decade mean divided by first-decade mean. Count only wildfire events (Incid_Type = 1).
entries.response:
The mean annual number of distinct wildfire events (Incid_Type = 1) increased from 255 in the first decade of the record to 401 in the last decade, a ratio of approximately 1.57. 

| First Decade Mean (1984-1993) | Last Decade Mean (2013-2022) | Ratio (Last / First) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 255.0 | 401.0 | 1.573 |

This indicates that there were roughly 57% more distinct wildfire events annually in the most recent decade compared to the 1984-1993 period.
